In iOS 27, Apple said it has paid special attention to making its software "more responsive, more reliable, and more delightful." This release includes multiple fix updates aimed at making your iPhone run faster, including an update targeting network switching.

iOS 27 makes switching between Wi-Fi and mobile networks smoother than ever

Apple said that, under the overarching goal of "platform improvements," they have done extensive work in iOS 27 to make your iPhone run faster.

The speed improvements are reflected in many areas, but one that Apple specifically highlighted is network switching.

In the past, whenever your iPhone switched between Wi-Fi and mobile networks, there was always an annoying delay.

When you step out of your home and move away from Wi-Fi range, your iPhone still thinks it is connected to Wi-Fi, so it cannot switch to mobile network immediately.

The result is that you will briefly be in a state with no data connection at all.

When encountering this situation, one common workaround is to open Control Center and temporarily turn off Wi-Fi, forcing the iPhone to switch to mobile network immediately.

But with iOS 27, you should no longer need to do this.

Apple stated: "During network switching, transitions between mobile network and Wi-Fi are smoother than ever."

Essentially, iOS 27 makes your iPhone smarter at determining when to switch from Wi-Fi to mobile network, and vice versa. And after months of beta testing, it seems Apple has indeed delivered on this.

So far, I can hardly recall needing to manually turn off Wi-Fi in iOS 27. Even during network switching, my iPhone maintains a stable connection. Hopefully, when iOS 27 is officially released, all users will enjoy the same experience.

How has your network switching experience been while using the iOS 27 beta? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
